items.root_cause: Two mechanisms, both measured over the window. (1) The emitter treated every move of the cheapest past 40 percent as an event about a price, and nothing asked whether the previous board already accounted for it: 32 of its 124 wow flags were only the SET of rows on the cell changing (an everyday crown dropping off the cell, or being undercut by a store back at its own last price) while the new cheapest was a price the board already carried; on 2026-09-17 alone that was 14 of 30. (2) The alert's unit is the day's batch, so any day that brings one new outlier or one unexplained move re-opens the type and scores as a RETURN of yesterday's close however right that close was; the outlier arm, where every confirmed defect of the window lived, has no referent that could explain one away (0 of 677 paging instances carry a store unit price).

root_fix.what: for (1): an explanation filter at the emitter. A wow move is recorded as the quiet type 'wow-explained' only when the previous board accounts for BOTH ends: the new cheapest is the same item at the same 4 dp per-unit its store carried on the previous board (or, for a store absent from it, the store's LAST recorded per-unit within the publish window), AND the old cheapest is still on the cell at the same price or has left the cell as an EVERYDAY row. A sale row leaving, a new price at the cheapest store, a same-item price change and a previous board that cannot be read or disagrees with the history all stay 'wow' and carry their reason. No threshold moved; the outlier arm is untouched. For (2): no build; it is the ruling Q-fccb69-unit-of-triage.
root_fix.exact_change: sanity-check.ps1: -PriorBoardDir (default: beside -CompareFile); the history pass keeps each commodity's previous entry and a per-store LAST per-unit bounded by the board's max_publish_age_days; new pure Get-WowExplanation (with Get-PriorBoardRow, Get-CellStoreRow, ConvertTo-PerUnitKey = integer count of 0.0001s); the wow branch writes type 'wow-explained' or 'wow' and appends ' - explained: ...' or ' - unexplained: ...' to the detail; one console line counts explained of all moves. check-ad-cycles.ps1 SANITY-PAGER region: $SANITY_QUIET += 'wow-explained', a per-type quiet count, and the log and summary lines name each quiet type instead of calling them all store-verified outliers. test-auditors.ps1: unit u144.

prevention.what: the fix is at the emitting check and its pager, not in any rule or exclusion file: the flag now asks the previous board whether the move is a change in which rows are on the cell before it pages, so the store churn that produced a quarter of the wow flags (and more than half of fccb69's listed ones) is recorded and never paged, while every move carrying a new price, a same-item change or a sale ending still pages with its reason

items.resolution_note: Root cause at the emitter, measured over 18 board versions: a quarter of the wow flags (32 of 124; 14 of 30 on 2026-09-17, 8 of fccb69's 11 listed) were a store dropping off the cell and a standing price taking the crown, not a price event. sanity-check now records those as 'wow-explained' and does not page them; every move with a new price, a same-item change or a sale row leaving still pages and says why. The dispatch's 'a sale ending is not a flag' was refused on the measurement: the confirmed 2026-09-07 laundry-pods defect (a fuel-saver price published for a week) was visible only as the move up when its sale row left. All four confirmed defects of the window and the bouillon basis error still page in frozen fixtures. Effect: pager-visible flags 801 -> 769, simulated NEW flags 149 -> 129 (one version rose 3 -> 7, displaced two days), days that page 15 -> 15 of 17: the type will keep firing, because new outliers arrive most days and a batch alert scores each day as a return (ruling Q-fccb69-unit-of-triage). No board or feed change, no republish.
items.premise_verified: true in part, false in part, checked 2026-09-21. TRUE: it is a RETURN, closed confirmed on 09-10, 09-11 and 09-18 (ops/out/events.jsonl), and the census adds 09-07 and 09-09. FALSE: 'the three confirmed closes were the defects' - 61f76c's two flags were real prices, so the three closes hold two defects (coconut, shrimp), both wrong products. PARTLY: hypothesis (a) - 107 of 124 wow were moves up, but only 32 of 124 are accounted for by the previous board, and its two named explanations (a sale ending; a crown change) would together have hidden the confirmed 09-07 laundry defect. FALSE: hypothesis (b) for the paged set - 0 of 677 paging outlier instances carry a store-published unit price; the 401 that do have been quiet as outlier-verified since 2026-09-04, and the log's '30 store-verified outlier(s) ... not paged' is exactly those.
items.deviation: Narrower than the dispatch's target shape, on measurement. (i) A sale ending is NOT an explanation: 11 of 124 wow were sale endings and one was the only trace of the 09-07 laundry defect. (ii) A crown change is an explanation only when the new cheapest is a price the board already carried and the old one was undercut or left as an everyday row; a crown moving to a NEW price is exactly the coconut defect. (iii) The per-condition pattern of plan-2026-09-21-5.json was NOT applied: a flag is already its own condition in this emitter (alerted-flags.json keys each commodity|type with its own clock), a queue type per flag would multiply the daily review items from 1 to a mean of 7.6 (max 26 on 2026-09-17) over the window, and a split by kind would not make a close stick because each kind's closes were different mechanisms. That is a cost ruling, filed as Q-fccb69-unit-of-triage, and it would also confound the before/after of this change. (iv) Two findings filed weekly: 2026-09-21-57e5ae (this item's residual) and 2026-09-21-594c27 (the RETURN gate is blind to 169 archived in-window closes).
